body.x: A robot cell or AMR route that looks sound on a drawing can still run into trouble once it is on the factory floor. Interference between machines, blocked travel paths and slow cycle times often come to light only after the equipment is installed, when changing the layout costs the most.
What if those problems could be found in a virtual environment first?

That is the approach taken by ST&I Co., Ltd., a company in Suseong-gu, Daegu, that supplies industrial software and 3D process simulation for smart factories. Led by CEO Heechang Kim, the company will take part in FIX 2026 through the 15th Daegu International Robot Industry Expo (ROBEX 2026). It says its purpose is to promote its smart factory and 3D simulation solutions, find potential customers and explore new business opportunities.

ST&I describes its work as covering the full smart factory process. It says it uses 3D manufacturing simulation to check industrial robots, autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), humanoid robots and other automation equipment in a virtual environment before they enter production. The items it verifies include equipment layout, logistics routes, robot workspaces, the possibility of interference and collisions, process flow and cycle times. According to the company, this reduces the trial and error and the implementation risk that come with introducing automation, and it supports process design and smart factory consulting that take productivity and space utilization into account.

The company also develops industrial gateways and smart factory monitoring systems. ST&I says these communicate with CNC machines, programmable logic controllers (PLCs), six-axis robots and sensors, collect and normalize the data, and bring production status, equipment conditions and operating information into one integrated view. The company describes its service as running from 3D process simulation and pre-validation through process design and consulting, infrastructure deployment, data collection and normalization, and integrated monitoring and operational support.

At the exhibition, ST&I will present integrated smart factory solutions built on IDEX, FIVAS and Visual Components. IDEX, in the company's description, is an industrial data acquisition gateway that collects and normalizes data from CNC machines, PLCs, robots, sensors and other equipment. FIVAS is an integrated platform that monitors production and equipment status in real time from the collected data and provides a digital twin environment. Visual Components is a 3D process simulation solution that validates the layout, movement paths, interference and cycle times of robots, AMRs, humanoid robots and other automation equipment before actual implementation.

ST&I says it has supplied and applied manufacturing process and robot automation simulation solutions to companies in a range of industries, including LG Energy Solution, Samsung Display, Hyundai Robotics and Hanwha Ocean. It also says it has introduced the solutions at major Korean research institutes, namely the Daegu Mechatronics & Materials Institute (DMI), the Korea Textile Machinery Convergence Research Institute (KOTMI) and the Korea Institute of Robotics & Technology Convergence (KIRO), where they support research, development and validation in manufacturing automation, robotics and digital twin technology.

ST&I currently has no exports. The company wants to enter the U.S. market for manufacturing plants and logistics automation. It says the U.S. is seeing active reshoring of manufacturing and automation investment, with continuing demand for industrial robots, AMRs, digital twins and smart factory solutions. ST&I plans to apply its 3D process simulation, manufacturing data collection and digital twin technology to the automation and pre-validation of distribution centers and factories there.

The company names local knowledge as its main obstacle. Working at overseas sites requires an understanding of the local manufacturing and logistics environment, a way to find customers, and a network of local system integrators and automation specialists. ST&I also lists technical support, maintenance, system integration standards and local requirements as areas where it needs partnerships.

Its plan is to propose 3D process simulation and smart factory solutions to U.S. manufacturers, distribution centers and automation solution companies, and to work with local partners to secure proofs of concept (PoCs) and reference projects. After that, the company intends to expand into robot- and AMR-based logistics automation, digital twins and manufacturing data integration to build a lasting business base in the U.S. market.

Now in its third year, FIX 2026 (Future Innovation Technology Expo) is a future-industry exhibition that brings together and connects innovative technologies in future mobility, robotics, AI and ICT, and startups. It runs from Wednesday, Oct. 21, to Saturday, Oct. 24, at EXCO in Daegu. Under the theme "AI, Beyond Tech into Reality," the show shares industry trends and core technologies through AI-based technology exhibitions, conferences and lectures by Korean and international experts, and networking programs.
